explanations: terra: The God-conscious establish prayer as an identifying act; 2:5 names this community as the successful, reproducing the section's prayer-to-success relation.
terra: “These are the successful” supplies the outcome of the prayer and faithful response described in 2:3-4.

luna: This command joins establishing prayer and giving zakat with bowing among those who bow, a concrete bodily act in the section's definition of human salat. | terra: The command to establish prayer is immediately embodied as وَٱرْكَعُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ, displaying bowing as part of communal salat.
terra: People recite the Book yet forget themselves while ordering others to righteousness; 2:45 turns immediately to prayer, exposing the failure to convert recitation into embodied practice.

luna: Believers are told to seek help through patience and prayer, which is difficult except for the humble who expect to meet their Lord; this connects salat to the section's humility and fear. | terra: Seeking help through patience and prayer follows the rebuke of reciters who forget themselves in 2:44; prayer is the difficult enacted answer except for the humble.

luna: The ayah condemns those who bar God's name from being mentioned in mosques and seek their ruin; it reverses the worship-house scene of 24:36, where the name is remembered and God glorified. | terra: Preventing God's name from being remembered in His mosques and seeking their ruin reverses the section's scene of the divine name voiced in places of prostration.

luna: Abraham and Ishmael are commanded to purify the House for those who circle it, stay there, bow, and prostrate; this links sacred place, purification, and the bodily acts in the section's prayer definition. | terra: God's house is purified for circumambulation, retreat, bowing, and prostration; a purified place gathers the bodily acts that the section's prayer definition enumerates.
luna: The Messenger recites God's verses, purifies the believers, and teaches them the Book and wisdom; this directly joins recitation and purification as the section does across 87:14-15.

luna: Remember Me; I will remember you, and be grateful to Me. The ayah directly connects dhikr with gratitude, another sense listed in the section's dictionary entry. | terra: فَٱذْكُرُونِىٓ أَذْكُرْكُمْ joins commanded remembrance to reciprocal divine remembrance and immediately to gratitude, one of the acts included in the section's dictionary definition of dhikr.

luna: The patient receive صلوات from their Lord and mercy. This is a divine-side use of the salat root, though whether it carries the section's specific sense of purification here is uncertain. | terra: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَٰتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ gives salat a divine subject and human recipients, exemplifying the root's direction from God toward His servants.
luna: After completing the rites, people are told to remember Allah with abundant remembrance; it makes remembrance the continuation of bodily worship, as 87:15 joins remembrance and prayer.

luna: The command to guard the prayers and stand قانتين makes the standing posture explicit, matching the section's bodily definition of salat. | terra: Guarding the prayers is followed by وَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ, making upright bodily standing an element of sustained prayer.

luna: In fear, prayer may be performed on foot or riding; when safe, believers are told to remember Allah. This ayah's own contribution is the bodily adaptation of salat and its transition to remembrance in safety. | terra: Under fear prayer may be performed walking or riding; once safe, remembrance resumes, joining bodily adaptation of salat to taught dhikr.
terra: Zechariah calls upon his Lord for good offspring; his supplication becomes standing salat in 3:39 and remembrance-tasbih in 3:41, illustrating the dictionary claim that prayer is dua.

luna: Zakariya is standing in prayer in the sanctuary when the angels call to him; the verse shows the bodily stance included in the section's definition of salat. | terra: Zechariah is قَآئِمٌۭ يُصَلِّى فِى ٱلْمِحْرَابِ when the angels call; this embodies prayer as standing and follows his supplication in 3:38.

luna: Zakariya is told to remember his Lord much and glorify Him morning and evening, combining the section's linked roots in a single prophetic instruction. | terra: Zechariah is commanded to remember his Lord much and glorify at evening and morning, extending the prayer and supplication scene of 3:38-39 into dhikr and tasbih.

luna: Mary is told to prostrate and bow with those who bow; the verse supplies the bodily gestures that the section's dictionary gives for prayer. | terra: Mary is commanded to be devout, prostrate, and bow with those who bow, gathering distinct prayer movements in one instruction.
terra: The signs God recites to the Prophet are also called ٱلذِّكْرِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ, directly grounding the section's dictionary sense of Qur'an recitation as dhikr.
terra: An upright community recites God's signs during the night وَهُمْ يَسْجُدُونَ, joining voiced recitation with the bodily movement of prayer.
luna: The Messenger recites verses, purifies believers, and teaches them the Book and wisdom; it makes the section's Quran-recitation and purification link explicit.

luna: These believers remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides, postures that overlap the section's bodily account of prayer while showing remembrance continuing through ordinary positions. | terra: These believers remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides, then voice a supplication; dhikr, bodily positions, reflection, and dua form one continuous worship scene.
luna: The passage asks about those who claim purity and answers that Allah purifies whom He wills, a direct contrast to treating 87:14's tazkiya as self-congratulation.
luna: This ayah permits shortening prayer during travel when believers fear attack; 4:102 supplies the following bodily arrangement for prayer in danger.

luna: The battle prayer divides worshippers into groups, with one group prostrating while another stands guard. The section's dictionary defines creaturely salat through bodily acts including standing and prostration. | terra: The prayer under danger is enacted by standing with the Prophet, taking arms, prostrating, and yielding place to another group; salat is visibly a coordinated sequence of bodily acts.

luna: After prayer, believers are told to remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on their sides; it connects salat and dhikr while showing remembrance continues beyond the bodily prayer. | terra: When prayer is completed, remembrance continues standing, sitting, and lying down; the verse binds salat, dhikr, and bodily positions before prayer is re-established in safety.

luna: Hypocrites stand for prayer lazily, show off, and remember God only a little; this directly reverses the section's remembrance and prayer as one attentive practice. | terra: Hypocrites rise lazily to prayer, display themselves, and remember God only a little; their standing reproduces prayer's body while severing it from sincere dhikr.
luna: The phrase الجهر بالسوء من القول uses the section's root ج ه ر for public speech, though its context concerns public evil words rather than audible prayer.
terra: The summons “when you rise to prayer” introduces washing of face and limbs, and the verse closes with God's desire to purify the believers; bodily preparation and purification surround salat.
terra: When believers make the public call to prayer, others turn it into mockery and play; the audible summons to salat receives the opposite of a worshipful response.
luna: This ayah names intoxicants, gambling, altars, and divining arrows as things to avoid; 5:91 explains their specific effect of diverting people from remembrance and prayer.

luna: The ayah says Satan uses intoxicants and gambling to turn people away from ذكر الله and الصلاة, naming the very pair the section joins and showing a force that breaks their practice apart. | terra: Satan's aim is to obstruct both عَن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ وَعَنِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ; the paired obstruction confirms that remembrance and prayer belong to one practice.
luna: God is said to know your secret and your public speech; the exact جهر/secrecy opposition echoes 87:7's known public and hidden speech.
luna: The Prophet must not dismiss those who call on their Lord morning and evening for His face or follow the heedless; this parallels the section's regular worship and warning against distraction.
terra: People call on God humbly and secretly in the darkness of land and sea, supplying another quiet-voice scene for prayer understood as dua.
terra: The prophetic message is described as a reminder to all peoples, supporting the section's inclusion of revealed recitation within dhikr.
terra: The command to set one's face at every place of prostration and call upon God sincerely joins bodily orientation, worship space, and prayer as dua.

luna: Believers are told to call on their Lord humbly and privately; it meets the section's dictionary sense of salat as supplication and its public/private speech detail. | terra: ٱدْعُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً stages dua in humility and privacy, supplying the quiet side of prayer as uttered supplication.
luna: The call to invoke God in fear and hope gives supplication the same fear stance that the section links to remembering the reminder.
terra: Those who hold firmly to the Book and establish prayer are joined in one description, making scriptural adherence and salat one enacted practice.

luna: When the Quran is recited, listeners are told to listen and be quiet for mercy; it makes the section's recitation-as-remembrance a shared act of hearing. | terra: When the Qur'an is recited, listeners are commanded to attend and be silent; it supplies the receptive counterpart to voiced reading as worship.
terra: The command joins inward, humble remembrance with speech below full loudness, دُونَ ٱلْجَهْرِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ, and ends وَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْغَٰفِلِينَ, opposing heedless worship.

luna: Those near their Lord do not disdain worship, glorify Him, and prostrate to Him; the verse directly combines the section's broad tasbih sense with a bodily act of prayer. | terra: The angels neither disdain worship nor tire: they glorify God and prostrate to Him, completing 7:205's quiet remembrance with tasbih and bodily submission.
luna: When God is mentioned, believers' hearts tremble, and recited signs increase their faith; it gives the section's remembrance and recitation a specific inward response.

luna: In the scene of meeting an enemy force, believers are told to remember Allah much so that they may prosper, joining abundant dhikr to success as 87:14-15 do. | terra: In the embodied pressure of battle, believers are commanded to remember God abundantly لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ, directly linking dhikr with success.

luna: The maintainers of God's mosques establish prayer, give zakat, and fear God alone; it is a positive counterpart to 24:36-37's worship-house and undistracted men. | terra: Those who maintain God's mosques are marked by established prayer, zakat, faith, and reverence, joining worship place, salat, and purification-giving.
terra: The hypocrites come to prayer only lazily; outward attendance without willing worship is a concrete boundary around the section's integrated practice.
terra: The sincere Bedouin treats his spending as nearness to God and as a means to صَلَوَٰتِ ٱلرَّسُولِ, showing salat as supplication offered for another person.

luna: The Prophet is told صل عليهم after charity that purifies its givers; their prayer is called reassurance. This joins the section's two directions, purification and a human salat that includes supplication. | terra: The command joins charity that purifies and increases purity, تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِم, with the Prophet's prayer over its givers, وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ; it closely parallels the section's purification-salat link.
luna: The ayah describes a mosque where the Prophet is to stand and men who love purification; it directly meets the section's bodily prayer and salat-as-tazkiya strands.

luna: The faithful are described as praising God, bowing, and prostrating; this directly joins praise to the bodily acts that the section includes in salat. | terra: The faithful are worshippers and praisers as well as ٱلرَّٰكِعُونَ ٱلسَّٰجِدُونَ, combining verbal devotion with prayer's bowing and prostration.

luna: The people of Paradise begin their دعوى with سبحانك اللهم and end it with الحمد لله; this directly gathers tasbih, supplication, and praise, which the section's dictionary lists under dhikr. | terra: The inhabitants of Paradise begin their supplication with سُبْحَٰنَكَ ٱللَّهُمَّ and end with praise, joining dua, tasbih, and praise as one uttered worship act.
terra: A suffering person calls on God lying, sitting, or standing, then passes on as though never having called; the same bodily positions that can sustain dhikr here frame forgotten supplication.

luna: The command to establish prayer at the day's edges is followed by the claim that good deeds remove wrong and that this is a reminder for those who remember, directly joining salat and dhikr. | terra: Prayer is commanded at the two ends of day and near night, and good deeds remove evil deeds; its repeated daily form is assigned a cleansing moral effect.
terra: The message for which the Prophet asks no payment is “only a reminder to all peoples,” another direct identification of revelation with dhikr.
luna: The verse contrasts one who conceals speech with one who proclaims it; this matches the section's public/private wording around الجهر, though the speech here is not specifically prayer.
luna: The verse says hearts find rest in remembrance of God, a specific effect of dhikr that complements the section's account of remembering as an act.

luna: Abraham asks to be made one who establishes الصلاة, then separately asks that his دعاء be accepted. The section's dictionary also lists supplication as a sense within salat; this verse clarifies the neighboring uses. | terra: Abraham's supplication asks God to make him and his descendants establish prayer, then asks that his dua be accepted; salat and supplication meet inside one prayer.

luna: The ayah calls the revelation الذكر and promises its preservation; alongside 87:6's promise that the Prophet will not forget, it presents divine keeping of the reminder. | terra: God calls the sent-down revelation ٱلذِّكْرَ and promises to guard it, supplying the object whose reading the section counts as remembrance.

luna: After distress at what people say, the Prophet is told to glorify his Lord with praise and be among those prostrating; this joins verbal praise with the bodily prayer named in the section. | terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ directly places glorification and prostration in one commanded act.
terra: God says وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلذِّكْرَ so the Prophet may explain what was sent, identifying the recited revelation itself as dhikr.

luna: All creation glorifies God with praise, extending the section's dictionary definition of tasbih as worship beyond spoken human praise; the verse itself is about creation's response. | terra: Everything glorifies God's praise although humans do not understand its tasbih; the ayah expands glorification beyond audible words while preserving it as a real act.

luna: The command to establish prayer is followed by Quran recitation at dawn, where the recitation is witnessed; the ayah directly puts salat and recitation together at appointed times. | terra: The command to establish prayer names قُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ within its daily span, making Qur'an recitation an expressly prayer-shaped act.
luna: The Prophet is told to keep a night vigil as an additional devotion; it supplies a specific bodily prayer practice within the section's account of salat.
luna: The Quran is divided so the Prophet may recite it to people over time; this gives a concrete public form to the section's claim that Quran reading is remembrance.

luna: When Quran is recited to people given knowledge, they fall prostrate; this directly stages the section's recitation and bodily salat together. | terra: When the revelation is recited, the knowledgeable fall on their chins in prostration; 17:108 supplies their spoken glorification.

luna: Their prostration is followed by declaring their Lord's promise true and praising Him; the response moves from bodily prayer to verbal praise. | terra: Their response within the recitation-prostration scene is سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّنَا, so the tongue's tasbih accompanies the body's fall described in 17:107.

luna: The passage closes with weeping prostration and increased humility, specifying the inward result of the recitation scene begun in 17:107. | terra: They again fall on their chins, now weeping and increasing in humility; the ayah completes the bodily effect of recitation and spoken glorification in 17:107-108.

luna: The command ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها gives a precise boundary for audible prayer. It activates the section's dictionary entry for جهر as making speech, prayer, and recitation audible. | terra: وَلَا تَجْهَرْ بِصَلَاتِكَ وَلَا تُخَافِتْ بِهَا sets an audible middle course for prayer, directly realizing the section's dictionary sense of جهر in prayer and recitation.

luna: The instruction واذكر ربك إذا نسيت directly connects remembrance of the Lord with forgetting, clarifying the section's reading of 87:6-7. | terra: وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ makes remembrance the direct remedy when forgetting occurs, clarifying the section's movement between being made to recite, not forgetting, and remembering.

luna: The faithful invoke their Lord morning and evening, while the warning is not to prefer worldly adornment or follow one heedless of ذكر الله. It reverses the section's undistracted remembrance amid trade. | terra: The Prophet must not obey one whose heart has been made heedless of God's remembrance, marking inward heedlessness as the opposite of sustained dhikr.

luna: Zakariya calls on his Lord with a private call, a specific scene of supplication and hidden speech that joins the section's dua and public/private details. | terra: Zechariah calls his Lord نِدَآءً خَفِيًّا, a concrete private-voice counterpart to the section's discussion of prayer or recitation made aloud.
luna: Zakariya signals to his people to glorify God morning and evening; this depicts tasbih as enacted communication and a repeated daily practice.

luna: When the Merciful's signs are recited, earlier prophets fall prostrate and weep; this joins recitation to bodily submission as the section joins reminder and prayer. | terra: When the Merciful's signs are recited, the prophets fall سُجَّدًا وَبُكِيًّا; hearing revelation immediately becomes embodied worship.

luna: The successors are said to have let prayer go to waste and followed desires, the direct contrary of remembering the Lord and praying in 87:15. | terra: Later generations neglect prayer and follow desires; the verse presents loss of salat as the breakdown of the integrated practice.
terra: The revelation is made easy بِلِسَانِكَ so the Prophet can announce good news and warning; it supports the section's movement from facilitated recitation to words circulating on the tongue.
luna: The Quran was sent as a reminder for one who fears; this directly joins recitation and fear, the two responses linked in 87:6 and 87:10.

luna: The verse says that if the Prophet speaks aloud, God knows what is secret and more hidden; this closely mirrors 87:7's knowledge of الجهر and what is hidden. | terra: If speech is made public, God knows the secret and what is still more hidden; this closely parallels the section's aloud-hidden boundary around voiced worship.

luna: Musa is told أقم الصلاة لذكري, making remembrance the stated purpose of prayer, just as the section joins the two acts. | terra: God commands Moses, وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِى, making prayer an enacted form and purpose of remembrance.
terra: Moses asks that the knot in his tongue be untied; 20:28 states the speech purpose, and 20:33-34 later names abundant tasbih and dhikr as the mission this speech serves.
terra: “That they may understand my speech” gives the purpose of the freed tongue in 20:27 before Moses names glorification and remembrance in 20:33-34.

luna: In Musa's request that Harun share his task, the purpose كي نسبحك كثيرا is collective glorification; the section likewise treats tasbih as part of a shared devotional practice. | terra: Moses asks for Aaron's aid so that “we may glorify You much”; 20:34 gives the paired purpose of remembering God much.

luna: The same request continues with ونذكرك كثيرا: Musa pairs frequent remembrance with the glorification in 20:33, directly echoing the section's linked verbs. | terra: وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا completes 20:33's abundant glorification and shows the two verbal acts as one shared mission.
luna: The gardens are the reward of one who purifies himself; this links the section's tazkiya bridge between 87:14 and 87:15 to an explicit promised outcome.
terra: The Arabic Qur'an varies its warnings so that hearers may become reverent or it may produce remembrance in them, directly joining recitation, fear, and new dhikr.
terra: The Prophet is told not to hurry the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to him, setting disciplined reception around the recitation God promises to secure.
luna: Whoever turns away from God's remembrance is promised a constricted life and blindness on the Day of Resurrection, a direct reversal of 87:10's remembering person who fears.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord before sunrise and sunset and at night; it is a direct counterpart to the section's opening imperative and its timed worship scenes. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord's praise before sunrise and sunset and at portions of night and day, giving the practice a prayer-like daily rhythm.
terra: The heavenly servants glorify night and day without slackening, another direct formulation of worship untouched by interruption or heedlessness.
luna: This ayah names Moses and Aaron's revelation as light and a reminder for the God-fearing, connecting the section's reference to Moses with Quranic remembrance.
luna: This ayah's own contribution is identifying the righteous as those who fear their Lord unseen and dread the Hour; 21:48 supplies their reminder from Moses and Aaron.

luna: The revealed scripture is called a blessed ذكر, linking the section's recitation to a transmitted reminder. | terra: The revealed scripture is هَٰذَا ذِكْرٌۭ مُّبَارَكٌ, supporting remembrance as engagement with the Qur'an rather than only an independent formula.
terra: Jonah's cry from darkness includes سُبْحَٰنَكَ inside his supplication, making glorification itself the language of prayer in distress.
terra: The purified House is assigned to those circling, standing, bowing, and prostrating, staging worship through its named places and movements.
luna: Every community is given a rite so that its people may mention Allah's name over the provision of livestock; this links remembrance of the Lord's name to embodied worship and provision.
luna: Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned are described as patient, establishing prayer, and giving; it joins dhikr and salat in a lived response.
luna: The ayah says neither the animals' flesh nor blood reaches God, but piety does; it clarifies that an outward ritual act is not itself the inward worship emphasized by the section.
terra: The protected worship sites include prayer houses and mosques “in which God's name is remembered much”; the ayah joins sacred place, the salat word-family, and repeated naming of God.

luna: Believers are told to bow, prostrate, worship their Lord, and do good so that they may prosper. This gives concrete bodily content to the section's account of salat and links it to success. | terra: Believers are commanded to bow, prostrate, worship, and do good لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ; bodily prayer is directly tied to the success named beside prayer in the section.

luna: This ayah announces the believers' success; the next ayah specifies humility in prayer, making success and attentive salat a direct pairing like 87:14-15. | terra: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ states success, and 23:2 immediately identifies their humble prayer as its first concrete mark.

luna: This ayah's own contribution is humility within prayer; 23:1 frames that manner of salat as a mark of the successful believers. | terra: The successful believers are فِى صَلَاتِهِمْ خَٰشِعُونَ; prayer is the enacted disposition following the success announced in 23:1.

luna: The passage closes its description of believers by saying they guard their prayers, a specific form of sustained salat alongside the section's closing prayer act. | terra: The successful believers carefully guard their prayers, giving a positive boundary for the section's warning about people heedless of their prayer.
luna: The ayah says no one would be purified without God's favor, but Allah purifies whom He wills; it develops the divine-side purification linked to salat in the section.

luna: This is the worship-house setting just before 24:37: God's name is mentioned and He is glorified morning and evening. The next ayah adds remembrance, prayer, and almsgiving among men not distracted by commerce. | terra: In the raised houses, God's name is remembered and He is glorified morning and evening; this supplies the worship setting whose practitioners are described in 24:37.

luna: The ayah names ذكر الله and إقامة الصلاة among acts from which trade does not distract these men; it sets remembrance and prayer inside ordinary work. | terra: Trade does not distract these men from ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ or إِقَامِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ; with 24:36, remembrance, glorification, prayer, and the purification term zakat form the section's single practice.

luna: The ayah says every creature knows its صلاة and تسبيح. It extends the section's creaturely prayer and broad tasbih definitions beyond human bodily worship. | terra: Every creature is said to know صَلَاتَهُ وَتَسْبِيحَهُ, an explicit pairing that supports the section's treatment of prayer and glorification as one practice.
luna: When told to prostrate to the Merciful, the deniers ask who He is and turn away; it is a specific refusal of the bodily worship that the section includes in salat.

luna: The servants of the Merciful spend nights prostrating and standing, a clear scene of the bodily acts that the section lists within salat. | terra: The servants of the Merciful spend the night before their Lord سُجَّدًا وَقِيَٰمًا, pairing prostration and standing as one nightly practice.
terra: God sees the Prophet “when you rise”; 26:219 specifies his movement among those prostrating, together presenting worship as bodily motion under divine sight.
terra: The Prophet's movement among the prostrators completes 26:218's rising posture and closely matches the section's definition of prayer as a sequence of movements.

luna: The ayah joins Quran recitation to prayer, says prayer restrains wrongdoing, and calls ذكر الله أكبر. That cognate of the section's كبرى for the fire assigns greatness to remembrance instead. | terra: The command joins reciting the Book to establishing prayer, then names prayer's restraining work and ذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ; it directly fuses recitation, prayer, moral effect, and remembrance.

luna: The command glorifies God at evening and morning, a direct daily-rhythm counterpart to tasbih in the section and its 24:36 parallel. | terra: فَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ orders glorification across evening and morning; 30:18 completes the daytime cycle with praise.

luna: This ayah assigns praise to God and repeats evening, afternoon, and noon times; it supplies the praise-and-time frame around 30:17's glorification, while its own contribution is praise. | terra: وَلَهُ ٱلْحَمْدُ ... وَعَشِيًّا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ adds praise and the remaining daily times to 30:17's glorification.
terra: Those who establish prayer, give zakat, and are certain of the Hereafter enact the same prayer-purification cluster; 31:5 names their success.
terra: The worshippers described in 31:4 are explicitly the successful, again joining established prayer and purification-giving to falah.

luna: Those reminded by God's signs fall prostrate, glorify their Lord with praise, and are not arrogant; the ayah stages reminder, sujud, and tasbih as one response. | terra: Those reminded by God's signs fall prostrate and glorify their Lord's praise; reminder, bodily prayer, and tasbih become one response.
luna: The list of faithful men and women includes those who remember Allah much and promises forgiveness and reward, a repeated formulation of abundant dhikr.

luna: Believers are commanded to remember Allah with much remembrance, matching the section's dictionary sense of dhikr as something repeatedly running on the tongue. | terra: The believers are commanded to remember God abundantly; 33:42 adds glorification and 33:43 answers with God's own salat upon them.

luna: The adjoining command to glorify Allah morning and evening pairs tasbih with 33:41's remembrance, the same linked practice and daily rhythm developed in the section. | terra: وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا turns abundant remembrance in 33:41 into repeated glorification at set parts of the day.

luna: Here Allah يصلي عليكم to bring believers from darkness into light. This is the divine-side sense named in the section, where Allah's salat is described as purification, rather than a person's ritual prayer. | terra: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَلِّى عَلَيْكُمْ gives the other direction of the salat root: after human remembrance and glorification in 33:41-42, God and His angels turn toward the believers and bring them from darkness to light.

luna: Allah and the angels يصلون على النبي and believers are told to do so too; it displays the non-ritual salat sense named in the section, though the verse addresses the Prophet specifically. | terra: God and the angels perform salat upon the Prophet, then believers are commanded to perform salat upon him; one ayah displays the root's divine and human directions together.
luna: The ayah joins fear of God unseen, establishing prayer, and purification; it gathers the section's fear, salat, and tazkiya strands in one statement.

luna: Those who recite God's book and establish prayer hope for a trade that will not fail; it joins Quran recitation to prayer and recasts the commerce that cannot distract the men of 24:37. | terra: Those who recite God's Book and establish prayer are named in one sequence; the verse directly joins the section's reading and salat.

luna: The ayah says the Prophet was not taught poetry but that the message is ذكر and a clear Quran, directly naming Quran as remembrance. | terra: The revelation is explicitly ُذِكْرٌۭ وَقُرْءَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ, identifying reminder and Qur'an while excluding poetry.
terra: Jonah's having been among those who glorify is named as the condition of his rescue, complementing the actual tasbih within his supplication in 21:87.

luna: The Quran is invoked as ذي الذكر, a direct formulation of the section's dictionary claim that Quran recitation is dhikr. | terra: The oath by “the Qur'an possessed of remembrance” makes the recited scripture itself the bearer of dhikr.
terra: The Qur'anic proclamation is again described as a reminder to all peoples, preserving the identity between recited message and dhikr.
terra: A person calls his Lord in distress, then forgets what he had called for after receiving favor; it reverses prayerful remembrance preserved beyond the moment of need.

luna: The devoted person stands and prostrates through the night, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy; it brings the section's bodily prayer together with its one-who-fears motif. | terra: The devout worshipper passes the night سَاجِدًا وَقَآئِمًا while fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy, giving prayer its paired bodily postures and inward stance.
terra: The “best discourse” makes skins shiver and then soften, together with hearts, إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ; recited revelation becomes remembrance with an embodied effect.

luna: The Prophet is told to glorify his Lord with praise morning and evening after being told to be patient; it directly joins tasbih, praise, and a daily rhythm. | terra: The Prophet is told to seek forgiveness and glorify his Lord's praise evening and morning, combining verbal worship with a repeated daily rhythm.
terra: “Call upon Me; I will answer you” is followed by calling that act عِبَادَتِى, giving a Qur'anic bridge for the section's dictionary statement that prayer is both dua and worship.
terra: The command forbids prostrating to the sun or moon and directs prostration to their Creator, drawing a boundary around the addressee of bodily worship.
terra: Those with the Lord glorify Him night and day without weariness; their unbroken tasbih is a counter-image to forgetful or heedless worship.
luna: Whoever is blinded from remembrance of the Merciful is assigned a devil as companion; it gives a specific consequence to the avoidance in 87:11.

luna: The revelation is called a ذكر for the Prophet and his people, a direct lexical counterpart to the section's account of Quran recitation as remembrance. | terra: The Qur'an is called ذِكْرٌۭ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ, making revelation a remembrance borne by the Prophet and his people.
terra: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ joins ease, the reciter's tongue, and remembrance, precisely developing the section's account of dhikr circulating on the tongue.
luna: A group of jinn listens to the Quran being recited and then returns to warn its people, showing recitation becoming remembrance shared with others.
terra: Believers are commanded to glorify God morning and evening, giving commanded tasbih the same repeated daily rhythm as prayer.

luna: The believers bear a sign on their faces from prostration, making the section's bodily prayer image visible in the body. | terra: The believers are seen رُكَّعًا سُجَّدًا seeking God's bounty and approval; bowing and prostration visibly mark their worship.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord before sunrise and sunset, a direct version of the section's opening command to glorify the Lord's name. | terra: The command to glorify with the Lord's praise before sunrise and sunset establishes the daily rhythm continued through night and prostration in 50:40.

luna: The command continues with night glorification and أدبار السجود, explicitly bringing tasbih together with prostration, one of the bodily acts in the section's salat definition. | terra: Night glorification and أَدْبَٰرَ ٱلسُّجُودِ explicitly place tasbih beside the embodied act of prostration.
luna: The Prophet is told to remind by the Quran those who fear God's warning, joining Quranic recitation, reminder, and fear as 87:9-10 do.
luna: The command وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين closely matches 87:9's charge to remind if the reminder benefits, naming the same work and its effect.

luna: The Prophet is told to be patient and glorify his Lord with praise when he rises; it connects glorification and praise to the section's devotional command. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord's praise حِينَ تَقُومُ; “when you rise” gives tasbih a bodily setting continued at night in 52:49.

luna: The instruction to glorify God at night and as stars set extends the preceding command into night worship, echoing the section's body-and-remembrance rhythm. | terra: Night and the retreat of the stars extend the glorification commanded in 52:48 across the worshipper's daily cycle.
luna: The passage describes one who turns away from God's remembrance and wants only worldly life, directly meeting 87:11 and the later contrast with worldly preference.
luna: The warning فلا تزكوا أنفسكم reverses 87:14's successful purification: the passage says God knows best who is truly mindful, clarifying that purification is not self-congratulation.
terra: فَٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِلَّهِ وَٱعْبُدُوا۟ closes the surah by converting an imperative into the body's prostration and worship.

luna: After the account of Noah's people, this ayah says the Quran is made easy for remembrance; it explicitly joins recitation and dhikr as the section's dictionary does. | terra: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ explicitly joins the Qur'an's being made easy with remembrance, bringing together the section's recitation, ease, and dhikr.

luna: After the account of Aad, the repeated claim that the Quran is easy for remembrance again names recitation as dhikr. | terra: The repeated formula that the Qur'an is made easy for remembrance makes recurrent practice, rather than a one-time hearing, part of the connection.

luna: After Thamud's destruction, the refrain that the Quran is easy for remembrance makes Quranic recitation the response to a warning. | terra: This third occurrence again identifies facilitated Qur'an engagement with dhikr, matching the section's inclusion of reading within remembrance.

luna: After the account of Lot's people, the same Quran-for-remembrance refrain confirms this connection across repeated warnings. | terra: The fourth refrain completes the surah-long insistence that the Qur'an has been made easy for remembrance.

luna: The direct command فسبح باسم ربك العظيم closely matches 87:1's command to glorify the name of the Lord Most High. | terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ is the closest formulaic parallel to the section's opening command, substituting the epithet “the Magnificent” for “the Most High.”

luna: The surah closes with the same command to glorify the name of the Lord Most Great, a second direct Quranic formulation of the section's opening act. | terra: The same command, فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ, returns near the surah's close, showing repeated glorification of the Lord's name as a framing act.

luna: Satan is said to make people forget remembrance of Allah; this gives the section's forgetting motif a direct contrary case. | terra: Satan makes a people forget ذِكْرَ ٱللَّهِ; this is the explicit reversal of remembrance preserved against forgetting.
luna: Those who forget Allah are made to forget themselves; this gives the section's remembrance and forgetting motif a direct reversal and consequence.
terra: After naming God's beautiful names, the ayah says all in the heavens and earth glorifies Him; divine name and universal tasbih meet in one statement.

terra: The surah opens with all creation glorifying God and later turns human listeners toward Friday prayer and remembrance in 62:9-10, echoing the section's structural movement from tasbih to enacted worship.

luna: The Messenger recites God's verses to people and purifies them before teaching the Book; this joins recitation and tazkiya, the two actions the section connects across 87:14-15. | terra: The Messenger recites God's signs and purifies his hearers; within the same surah, 62:9-10 turns that recited instruction into Friday prayer, remembrance, and success.

luna: At the Friday call to prayer, believers are told to hasten to ذكر الله and leave trade; this gives the section's remembrance-and-prayer pairing a concrete public setting. | terra: At the call to Friday prayer, believers are told فَٱسْعَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ; the congregational prayer itself is approached as remembrance.

luna: After prayer, the ayah permits dispersal for livelihood and commands abundant remembrance; it makes explicit the continuation of worship into ordinary activity. | terra: After the Friday prayer, abundant remembrance continues into ordinary movement and is tied to success, linking the section's remembrance-prayer sequence to فلاح.

luna: This ayah's own contribution is the crowd leaving the Messenger standing for trade and amusement, reversing the undistracted men of 24:37; 62:9-10 supply the preceding Friday prayer and remembrance commands. | terra: The congregation leaves the Prophet standing when trade or amusement appears, enacting the distraction that 62:9 forbids and reversing the undistracted worshippers of 24:37.

luna: Believers are warned not to let wealth and children distract them from ذكر الله, and those who do are called losers; this echoes the commerce that fails to distract the men in 24:37. | terra: Wealth and children must not distract believers from God's remembrance; those distracted are the losers, reversing the section's dhikr-to-success relation.

luna: The ayah allows believers to conceal or proclaim their speech and says God knows what is in their hearts, a close verbal parallel to 87:7's known public and hidden speech. | terra: Whether speech is concealed or made public, God knows what breasts contain; the ayah extends the جهر boundary from audible words to inward intention.
terra: They will be called to prostrate but will be unable; 68:43 explains that they had been called to prostration while sound, making the lost bodily response a judgment.
terra: They are called to prostration but cannot perform it, though they had been called while sound; bodily capacity without prior obedient practice has been lost.
terra: The unbelievers nearly strike the Prophet down with their looks لَمَّا سَمِعُوا۟ ٱلذِّكْرَ; dhikr here is an audible recitation, and 68:52 identifies its universal scope.
terra: وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ completes 68:51's scene of hearing, showing the recited message itself as remembrance.

luna: After defending the Quran as revelation, the ayah ends فسبح باسم ربك العظيم, again pairing glorification with the Lord's name as in 87:1. | terra: The surah closes with فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ, an exact structural analogue for worship organized around glorifying the Lord's name.
terra: Worshippers form the exception to the anxious, withholding human type described around them; 70:23 defines their distinguishing constancy in prayer.
terra: These worshippers are constant in their prayer, supplying a sustained positive counterpart to prayer marked by heedlessness.
terra: A second description says they guard their prayers, repeating the vigilance that distinguishes integrated worship from nominal salat.
terra: وَأَنَّ ٱلْمَسَٰجِدَ لِلَّهِ identifies prostration places as belonging to God and forbids calling upon another there, joining place, bodily worship, and dua.

luna: This ayah opens the instruction to stand in prayer through the night; 73:4 specifies measured Quran recitation within the same night practice. | terra: “Stand at night” supplies the bodily posture for the measured Qur'an recitation commanded in 73:4 and the remembrance and prayer later named in 73:8 and 73:20.
luna: This ayah sets the night prayer's duration at half the night or a little less; it gives the bodily practice in 73:2 a concrete measure.

luna: The Prophet is told to recite the Quran with measured recitation within the night vigil, explicitly combining prayer and Quran reading. | terra: The command to recite the Qur'an in a measured manner makes voiced reading the work performed during the night standing of 73:2 and completed by remembrance in 73:8.

luna: The Prophet is told واذكر اسم ربك and to devote himself wholly to God, directly meeting the section's mention of the Lord's name and remembrance. | terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ directly echoes remembering the Lord's name and presents it as undivided devotion.

luna: This long instruction puts Quran recitation, إقامة الصلاة, giving, and seeking forgiveness together; it concretely supports the section's claim that recitation and prayer belong to one devotional practice. | terra: فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ and وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ put feasible recitation and established prayer in the same concluding instruction.
luna: The command to magnify the Lord is a parallel devotional formulation to 87:1's glorification of the Lord's name, though it uses كبر rather than the section's root س ب ح.
luna: This ayah asks what brought people into Saqar; 74:43 gives their answer, that they were not among those who prayed. Its own contribution is to frame the fire as a question of conduct.

luna: Those questioned about entering Saqar answer that they were not among the people who prayed; this makes prayer's absence a direct contrast to the successful worshipper in 87:14-15. | terra: The people of the Fire confess that they were not among those who prayed, placing omitted prayer on the path to the punishment that the section contrasts with remembrance.

luna: The Quran is called a تذكرة, directly supporting the section's dictionary treatment of Quran recitation as remembrance. | terra: The revelation is called a reminder; 74:55 then turns that objective reminder into the hearer's voluntary remembering.

luna: The next ayah says فمن شاء ذكره: whoever wills may remember it, linking Quranic reminder with the remembering person in 87:10. | terra: “Whoever wills may remember it” states the human act elicited by the reminder named in 74:54.
luna: The passage concludes that they remember only if God wills, a specific parallel to 87:6-7's recitation, forgetting, and divine will.

luna: The Prophet is told not to move his tongue hastily while receiving revelation; this directly recalls 87:6's promised recitation and the section's link between recitation and remembrance. | terra: لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ addresses the physical tongue during reception of the Qur'an; 75:17-18 identify God's collecting and reciting followed by the Prophet's recitation.

luna: The ayah says collecting and reciting the revelation are God's responsibility, illuminating the section's statement that God will make the Prophet recite. | terra: God assumes responsibility for gathering the revelation and قُرْءَانَهُ, paralleling the promise that the Prophet will be made to recite without losing it.

luna: The Prophet is instructed to follow the Quran when it is recited, specifying the responsive act behind the section's Quran-recitation-as-dhikr gloss. | terra: When God has recited it, the Prophet is told فَٱتَّبِعْ قُرْءَانَهُ; divine imparting becomes the reciter's voiced following.
luna: The passage concludes that explaining the recitation is God's responsibility, completing the revelation sequence that 87:6 summarizes.
terra: The condemned person neither affirmed nor prayed; 75:32 pairs that failed salat with denial and turning away.
terra: Denial and turning away explain the absence of prayer in 75:31, making salat the bodily counterpart of affirming the message.

luna: The command واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا repeats the section's remembrance of the Lord's name and gives it a morning-evening rhythm. | terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ commands remembrance of the Lord's name morning and evening; 76:26 continues the same practice bodily.

luna: The ayah adds night prostration and lengthy glorification after 76:25's remembrance command, making bodily prayer and tasbih parts of one daily pattern. | terra: Night worship is staged as prostration followed by prolonged glorification, فَٱسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ, completing the named remembrance of 76:25 with bodily prayer.
terra: When commanded ٱرْكَعُوا۟ they do not bow, a direct reversal of prayer as obedient bodily movement.
luna: Musa asks Pharaoh هل لك إلى أن تزكى, a direct call to purification that echoes 87:14 and gives the section's tazkiya link a prophetic scene.
luna: Musa continues by offering to guide Pharaoh to his Lord so that he may fear Him; this joins guidance and fear as 87:3 and 87:10 do around the section's worship image.
luna: Pharaoh claims أنا ربكم الأعلى, reversing 87:1's command to glorify the Lord Most High by making himself the highest lord.

luna: The Quran is called a تذكرة, a direct match for the section's dictionary sense that reciting Quran is dhikr. | terra: The admonition is called a reminder; 80:12 immediately describes the person who chooses to remember it.

luna: The following ayah says فمن شاء ذكره; it describes the response to Quranic reminder that the section connects to the one who remembers. | terra: “Whoever wills may remember it” converts the revealed reminder of 80:11 into personal dhikr.
terra: The revelation is “only a reminder to all peoples,” a repeated formulation that makes Qur'an reception an act of remembrance.
terra: When the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate; the refusal reverses the recitation-to-prostration response in 17:107 and 19:58.
luna: The command فذكر إنما أنت مذكر directly parallels 87:9's instruction to remind and identifies the Prophet's role as reminder.
luna: This ayah says the reminder's bearer is not a controller over the people; 88:21 gives his task to remind and 88:23 describes those who turn away, so this verse sets the limit of the role.
luna: This ayah's own contribution is the person who turns away and disbelieves; 88:21 names the reminder he rejects, paralleling the avoidance in 87:11.

luna: The one who turns away and disbelieves is threatened with the greatest punishment, joining rejection of reminder to punishment as in 87:11-12; الأكبر also recalls the section's comparison with أكبر in 29:45.

luna: The near-verbatim claim قد أفلح من زكاها links success with purification, the two ideas joined in 87:14 just before the prayer the section discusses. | terra: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا reproduces the section's success-through-purification claim and helps explain why divine salat and human prayer are linked through تزكية.
luna: The soul's failure is its corruption, the reverse of 91:9's successful purification and 87:14's person who purifies himself.
luna: The most God-fearing person is spared the blazing fire, joining fear and escape from punishment as in 87:10-12, before the next ayah describes purification.
luna: This person gives wealth to purify himself; it parallels 87:14's successful purification while showing a distinct act through which purification is pursued.

luna: The first command to recite is اقرأ باسم ربك, joining Quran reading to the Lord's name as the section joins remembrance with the Lord's name. | terra: The surah opens with ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ and closes in 96:19 with prostration and nearness; its command-to-bodied-worship arc closely parallels this section's opening and completion.

luna: The passage asks about one who forbids a servant's prayer; it introduces a concrete obstruction to the bodily worship that the section describes. | terra: This ayah introduces the person who forbids; 96:10 supplies the forbidden object, a servant at prayer, so the row contributes the hostile act around that worship scene.

luna: This ayah specifies that the forbidden act is a servant's prayer, sharpening the contrast between interruption and the section's act of salat. | terra: The forbidden act is stopping عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّىٰ, placing a servant's actual prayer between the opening command to recite in the Lord's name and the closing command to prostrate.
luna: This continuation asks whether the servant being forbidden is on guidance; 96:10 identifies the interrupted act as prayer, so this ayah specifies the worshipper's stance.
luna: This ayah asks whether the praying servant enjoins mindfulness of God, continuing the contrast between the one who prays and the one who obstructs him.
luna: This continuation asks whether the one forbidding prayer denies and turns away; its own contribution is the opponent's refusal, completing the scene that begins in 96:9-10.
luna: The ayah asks whether the opponent knows that Allah sees him; it completes the prayer-obstruction scene and echoes the section's claim that God knows what is public and hidden.

luna: After a person forbids a servant's prayer, the command is كلا لا تطعه واسجد واقترب: prostration is the bodily approach that answers the attempted interruption of worship. | terra: وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب closes the surah by turning the opening recitation in the Lord's name into the servant's bodily worship.

luna: This verse directs woe at those identified as praying; 107:5 names their fault as heedlessness, so the passage distinguishes the rite from mindful remembrance. | terra: The warning to “those who pray” makes the prayer label alone insufficient; 107:5 identifies heedlessness toward their own prayer as the fault.

luna: These worshippers are heedless of their prayers; the section explicitly reads this as a form of forgetting, a reversal of its remember-and-pray closing act. | terra: عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ reverses the section's recitation without forgetting: a bodily prayer emptied by heedlessness is condemned.

luna: This ayah adds that they act to be seen, extending 107:4-5's warning about heedless prayer into ostentation; its contribution is the motive behind the neglect. | terra: “They show off” continues 107:4-5 by identifying the intention behind heedless prayer, distinguishing performed movements from sincere remembrance.
luna: The final ayah adds that they withhold even small aid, completing the passage's reversal of the section's prayer as an active practice of obedience.
terra: The closing command joins glorifying the Lord's praise with seeking His forgiveness, exemplifying tasbih as a broad verbal act of worship.
